etymologies.etymologyHTML: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from French s’allonger (“to lie down”). Compare French longer (“to walk along”). Compare also German lungern (“to hang or lounge around, linger”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To relax; to spend time lazily; to stand, sit, or recline, in an indolent manner.

quote.text: We lounge over the sciences, dawdle through literature, yawn over politics.

quote.citation: 1993, “Loungin'”, in Guru's Jazzmatazz, Vol. 1, performed by Guru ft. Donald Byrd:
quote.text: Everybody knows they have times when they wanna just lay back / Kick their feet up, y'know / Listen to some good music and just lounge / That's right, I said lounge

quote.citation: 2001, Salman Rushdie, Fury: A Novel, London: Jonathan Cape, →ISBN, page 4:
quote.text: On Professor Solanka’s street, well-heeled white youths lounged in baggy garments on roseate stoops, stylishly simulating indigence while they waited for the billionairedom that would surely be along sometime soon.

definitions.definition: To walk or go in a leisurely manner.

quote.citation: 1911, James George Frazer, The Golden Bough, volume 9, page 287:
quote.text: When this bejewelled exquisite lounged through the streets playing on his flute, puffing at a cigar, and smelling at a nosegay, the people whom he met threw themselves on the earth before him and prayed to him with sighs and tears.

quote.citation: 2023 August 24, Pauline Lester, Marjorie Dean College Sophomore, BoD - Books on Demand, →ISBN, page 47:
quote.text: As she lounged past Leila's car she cast an insolent glance at the Irish girl.

definitions.definition: (now rare) A place where one can lounge; an area, establishment, house etc. where loungers gather and where one can relax and be at ease.

quote.citation: 1791, Charlotte Smith, Celestina, Broadview, published 2004, page 196:
quote.text: He  […]  prevailed on Captain Musgrave to introduce him to a family, where he supposed he might find a monstrous good lounge for the rest of the time he was to be quartered in the neighbourhood.

quote.citation: 1803 (date written), [Jane Austen], Northanger Abbey; published in Northanger Abbey: And Persuasion. […], volume (please specify |volume=I or II), London: John Murray, […], 20 December 1817 (indicated as 1818), →OCLC:
quote.text: Every search for him was equally unsuccessful, in morning lounges or evening assemblies.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter II, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume II, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 16:
quote.text: One morning she accompanied Madame de Soissons to the fair, then the favourite lounge and amusement. The Comtesse bought every trifle that caught her eye, while Francesca looked on.

definitions.definition: The act of someone who lounges; idle reclining.

quote.text: That is, he devoted his waking hours to lounges among the habitués of Chestnut-street, and lollings in an arm-chair of 'Squire Coke in Walnut-street.

definitions.definition: (British) The living room or sitting room of a house.

quote.citation: 1954, Alexander Alderson, chapter 18, in The Subtle Minotaur‎[1]:
quote.text: The lounge was furnished in old English oak and big Knole settees. There were rugs from Tabriz and Kerman on the highly polished floor.  […]  A table lamp was fashioned from a silver Egyptian hookah.

definitions.definition: A large comfortable seat for two or three people or more, a sofa or couch; also called lounge chair.
A waiting room in an office, airport etc.
An establishment, similar to a bar, that serves alcohol and often plays background music or shows television.
